A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SENSE study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM experiments on GLUE, paraphrasing, simplification and WMT22, alongside attention visualizations and generated examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and additionally reports two natural-language inference cases comparing SENSE with vanilla prompting.

M1.justification: The semantic-hint prompting procedure and prompt templates remain unchanged (v1 Tables 7–8; v2 Tables 6–7). Explicitly describing SENSE as zero-shot clarifies the existing approach.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate seven GLUE tasks, QQP paraphrasing, TurkCorpus and GoogleComp simplification, and four WMT22 translation directions. The added inference examples illustrate an already-covered task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines, including CoT, SP-Input/SP-Output, BERT/RoBERTa, WMT-Best, GPT EVAL, DTG 5-shot and BayLing. The SR labels in v1 Appendix Table 10 match the SP methods in v2 Table 4.

E3.justification: Appendix A retains the dataset counts, metrics, API model versions, temperature 0, top_p 1 and prompt templates. The more specific LLaMA3-70B-Instruct identification does not establish a model switch, and no revised evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix A.3 and Table 10 add two inference case studies with ground-truth labels, predictions and explanatory analyses. Existing paraphrasing cases and attention analyses are retained; the detailed GLUE comparison is relocated from the appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed variation, confidence intervals or significance tests. The signed annotations added to v2 Table 4 represent differences from vanilla prompting rather than statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Retained per-task benchmark scores are identical. v2 Table 10 adds inference predictions: SENSE matches the first ground-truth label but predicts neutral against contradiction in the second. The CoT/SP-Input/SP-Output GLUE averages of 75.03/72.48/74.43 are omitted, while their task-level scores remain.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The retained metric descriptions and methodological reasoning introduce no changed mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: directly incorporating parsing results can harm LLM performance, while semantic-hint prompting improves understanding and generation. The added examples do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of the inference cases and presents them as evidence of better semantic understanding (Appendix A.3, Table 10). This includes defending a neutral prediction despite the stated contradiction label. Existing mechanism explanations and the limitations section remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies LLaMA3-70B-Instruct, states zero-shot use, and clarifies that parsing baselines use LLM-generated parses without prescribing a parsing type (Sections 2.1 and 3.2; Appendix A.2). These additions improve documentation without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kojima et al. (2022) for zero-shot chain-of-thought and Wang et al. (2019) for GLUE. The broader positioning relative to semantic parsing, prompt optimization and earlier prompting approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and explanatory edits, revises the appendix case-study discussion, adds an equal-contribution note and acknowledgements, and updates author contact text. The main section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the main average-only GLUE display with the relocated task-level comparison and colored deltas, merges v1 Tables 4 and 9 into Appendix Table 8, and adds an inference case table. Figure 1 is resized and its caption clarified; other figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: Clearer checkpoint and parsing-baseline documentation, together with easier inspection of task-level GLUE comparisons, provide a modest net benefit. The quantitative evidence remains unchanged. The new inference analysis overstates its support because one SENSE prediction disagrees with the supplied ground truth, limiting the value of that addition.
